Everything that is queued is running. The CPU quota is the limit, and disk space will run short in about 5 hours unless someone frees space on /raid.

- **Running:** 8 physrotS FEBio runs on the old queue, all healthy (every log written within the last 30 s), with 32 more waiting since 04:31. Since 02:00, 3 runs have finished.
- **CPU:** 25.7 of the 32-core quota in use, 2 % throttled. This is what limits speed.
- **GPUs:** my runs sit on GPUs 1–4 at about 3 GB each, near 0 % busy because the runs wait on CPU. GPUs 0, 5 and 6 are almost full with other users' jobs.
- **Memory:** 128.7 of 137.4 GB, but 105.7 GB of that is file cache; only 21.9 GB is held by processes, so there is no out-of-memory risk.
- **New repo task queue:** empty. Its 5 failed gate2 tasks are from 10-28 and were already known.
- **Services:** all tmux services are up. The three one-time chains are finished and marked done, so nothing needed restarting.

**Change:** the old rule said to pause new launches once /raid fell below 15 GB. It is at 12.2 GB, but I kept launches going. That rule was set for older runs of about 2.7 GB each; physrotS runs are about 0.4 GB. The new rule is to pause below 5 GB. I only edited the comment in the `h19_scheduler.py` settings block, so the scheduler did not need a restart.

**Disk:** /raid loses about 2 GB per hour with 8 runs going. The rest of the batch needs roughly 15 GB and only 12.2 GB is free.

**Needs a person:** free at least 10 GB on /raid so the batch can finish without pausing.
